body:
## Goal Bring **lexbor** into the build as a vendored submodule, and prove it links and parses with a smoke test. No integration into the browser window yet — this is a build-system spike. Per ADR-001 (HTML parsing = lexbor, vendored) and ADR-006 (return to ADR-001 after the custom parser experiment was abandoned). ## Steps to Complete 1. **Add lexbor as a git submodule** at `third_party/lexbor/`, pinned to a released tag (e.g. `v2.4.0`). - Verify that lexbor does *not* ship a top-level `CMakeLists.txt`. 2. **Write a CMake wrapper** for lexbor: - Add `third_party/CMakeLists.txt` (or `cmake/lexbor.cmake`). - Define a `lexbor` static library target from lexbor's `source/` files. - Export lexbor's public headers via `target_include_directories(lexbor PUBLIC ...)`. - Mark it `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL`. - If lexbor generates config headers at build time, replicate that in the wrapper (this is the main unknown — investigate first). 3. **Write a smoke test** at `tests/test_lexbor_smoke.cpp`: - Parse `

Hello

`. - Walk the resulting tree. - Assert the `

` text content is `"Hello"`. 4. **Wire into CMake:** - Add `test_lexbor_smoke.cpp` to the `honeybee_tests` target in `tests/CMakeLists.txt`. - Link `lexbor` into `honeybee_lib` (or the test target) as needed. 5. **Document the submodule** in `docs/getting-started.md`: contributors must clone with `--recursive` (or run `git submodule update --init --recursive`). ## Acceptance Criteria - `cmake --build build` succeeds from a clean checkout (after submodule init). - `ctest` passes, including the new `test_lexbor_smoke`. - CI (`Build and Test on Ubuntu`) passes. - No changes to `window.cpp` or `honeybee` executable behavior — this is infrastructure only. ## Out of Scope - Any real HTML -> text extraction logic (that's Phase 1). - Any integration with `HoneyBeeWindow` (that's Phase 2). - Cairo, layout, or paint (Phases 4-5). ## Learning Outcomes - How CMake wraps a C library that ships no CMake support. - How git submodules work in practice. - How lexbor represents an HTML tree (`lxb_html_document_t`, `lxb_dom_node_t`). - Why vendoring (vs. `FetchContent` vs. system package) matters for reproducibility. ## Notes for the Assignee The main risk here is lexbor's build system. It is Makefile-based and may generate headers at build time. **Investigate this before writing the wrapper.** If lexbor does ship a `CMakeLists.txt`, use it directly and skip the wrapper.
title: build(parser): vendor lexbor as submodule with CMake wrapper + smoke test
